title: MLP Architecture & Evolutionary Algorithm
lede: Technical specification of the neural network decision engine and the generational neuroevolution pipeline.

mlp.summary: Each animal is driven by a Multi-Layer Perceptron acting as its biological nervous system. Synaptic weights and bias arrays comprise the evolvable chromosome.

layers.name: Input Layer
layers.description: 5 Internal Status nodes + 36 Sensory Perception nodes (9 tiles in a 3x3 Moore neighborhood with 4 features per tile).

breakdown.details: Health (%), Hunger (%), Thirst (%), Energy (%), Instinct (0 for Calm, 1 for Alert)
Active hazard detected on tile (Fire, Flood, Toxic Cloud)
Edible sustenance present on tile (Flora or Prey)
Other animal agent located on tile

layers.name: Hidden Layer 1
layers.description: Primary feature synthesis layer, distilling sensory-internal correlation patterns.

layers.name: Hidden Layer 2
layers.description: Behavioral arbitration layer, resolving conflicting drives (hunger vs threat evasion).

layers.name: Output Layer
layers.description: Discrete motor action nodes. The node with highest activation determines the action for that turn.

evolution.summary: A continuous generational loop mimicking natural selection, translating individual survival into population-wide adaptation.

steps.name: Population Initialization
steps.detail: Generate an initial cohort of N animals with uniformly randomized synaptic weights sampled from a normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 0.5.

steps.name: Generational Simulation
steps.detail: Release the population into the 25x25 grid arena for a fixed duration of turns (or until total extinction). Animals act autonomously according to MLP forward passes.

steps.name: Fitness Evaluation
steps.detail: Compute the quantitative Fitness Score for each animal upon death or simulation conclusion using the designated multivariable formula.

steps.name: Elitism Retention
steps.detail: Directly copy the top 5% to 10% highest-scoring individuals (elites) into the next generational pool without mutation, preventing loss of peak adaptations.

steps.name: Parent Selection
steps.detail: Select breeding pairs using fitness-proportionate selection (roulette wheel) or tournament selection, ensuring higher fitness equates to higher reproductive probability.

steps.name: Crossover (Recombination)
steps.detail: Combine flattened weight matrices from two selected parents using single-point or uniform crossover to generate offspring chromosomes.

steps.name: Mutation (Genetic Drift)
steps.detail: Apply stochastic perturbation to offspring weights at a controlled mutation rate (typically 5% per gene), adding Gaussian noise (N(0, 0.1)) to prevent stagnation.
